//: ADR-019 D7. THE declared source of truth for notice types. Consumed by the DDL (the CHECK constraint on notices.notice.notice_type) and by the module's TypeScript union, both PROJECTED from here by `pnpm gen:notice-types` — never hand-listed. A type added here and nowhere else is a drift the --check step refuses.

general.description: An ordinary announcement with no operational consequence. The default, and deliberately first: a type system whose fallback is 'emergency' teaches people to downgrade.

planned_interruption.description: A scheduled loss of a service — water, lift, power. Distinguished from an emergency because it is KNOWN IN ADVANCE, which is what makes the schedule meaningful and the audience precise.

emergency.description: Unplanned and urgent. A separate type rather than a severity flag, because the operational handling differs: it is not scheduled, and it is not withheld pending approval.

event_community.description: A community event. Kept apart from 'general' because residents opting out of social announcements must not thereby opt out of operational ones.

//vocabularies: GEN-042 H2. The DISPOSITION vocabulary (what an actor DID) and the LIFECYCLE vocabulary (what state the notice is IN) are DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION. They used to share `approved` and `withdrawn`, and GEN-040 lost an afternoon to it: a state check written against a disposition literal type-checked and silently never matched, so every approval refused as wrong-state. Disjoint vocabularies make that comparison a TS2367 'no overlap' error instead of a false condition.

approval_requested.description: The author sent it for approval.

approval_granted.description: An approver agreed it may be published.

publication_released.description: It was published; the schedule then decides live/scheduled/expired.

withdrawal_recorded.description: It was withdrawn; the audience snapshot is retained.
